title: Mash-Step Temperature Hold Compliance
dataSources: Fermentation telemetry (`brew:fermentation`), brew-day records (`brew:batch`), mash probes (`brew:mash`), keg pressure (`kegerator:pressure`), tap pours (`kegerator:pour`), brew-fridge duty logs (`brewfridge:compressor`), cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`), and line-cleaning events (`tapline:clean`).
app: Homebrewing telemetry from Tilt/iSpindel fermentation sensors, Brewfather batch exports, ESPHome mash and fridge probes, keg pressure sensors, tap flow meters, and cellar climate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=brew:mash
| eval abs_delta=abs(temp_delta_c)
| stats avg(temp_delta_c) as avg_delta_c max(abs_delta) as max_delta_c by batch step_name
| sort batch step_name
description: Summarises how closely each mash step stayed on target temperature during the brew day.
value: Mash consistency drives extract and fermentability, so step compliance gives you a measurable way to improve repeatability from batch to batch.
implementation: Send target and actual mash temperatures from your controller or recipe app during each step of the mash schedule.
visualization: Table of average and worst temperature drift by mash step.
grandmaExplanation: It compares whether each mash step stayed near the planned temperature, which helps explain why one batch differs from another.
